name: as-any
description: `as any` erases the type checker at that expression — on money and multi-tenant paths that's where a mispriced charge or a cross-org data leak hides. `(req as any)` and `(req.user as any).id`-style casts have typed replacements (AuthenticatedRequest + req.user.id, getOrganizationId(req)); Express-internals monkey-patches are the residual baseline. This ratchet freezes the count and drives it strictly DOWN — lower baselineCount whenever a reduction lands.
lastBumpNote: 1300 -> 1288 on 2026-08-23 (measured, not estimated): the seven `(job as any)._dbId` reads in jobQueue.ts and the `(storage as any).redis` probes in customDomainRouter.ts. Neither was a ghost — both were real contracts carried outside the type system, which is what made them indistinguishable from reads of columns that do not exist. Declared `Job._dbId` on the interface and extracted a `DomainCacheRedis` seam. PRIOR NOTE — 1316 -> 1300 on 2026-08-23: the reported-financials fix removed SIXTEEN casts, not the nine I first wrote here — the ghost reads plus the spurious casts sitting beside them on columns that were real all along. Corrected to the measured count after the ratchet failed stale-high a second time; the number comes from the gate, not from an estimate. Deletion-revealed by the ghost-field gate, not a typing pass. PRIOR NOTE — 1323 -> 1316 on 2026-08-23: the seven `(invoice as any).subscription` reads in both invoice.payment_failed handlers (webhookHandlers.ts, stripeConnect.ts). The field is not on Stripe.Invoice in the pinned API version — it moved under parent.subscription_details — so the id was always undefined and every dunning event recorded '' for the subscription it belonged to. Replaced by the canonical invoiceSubscriptionId(), which returns null rather than '': in a nullable column, '' asserts there IS a subscription and it is blank. Deletion-revealed by the ghost-field gate. Locked in per the strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 1326 -> 1323 on 2026-08-23: the three `(sub as any).current_period_*` reads removed by the Stripe billing-period fix. Those fields are on the subscription ITEM in the pinned API version, not the subscription, so two of them were `new Date(NaN).toISOString()` — a RangeError thrown for every customer who actually had a subscription — and the third silently disabled a renewal prediction. Replaced by the canonical `subscriptionPeriod()` / `subscriptionPeriodIso()` in server/stripeClient.ts, adopted at all four sites. Locked in per the strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 1335 -> 1326 on 2026-08-23: nine casts went with the campaign-body fix in server/routes-campaigns.ts. Eight read templateContent / htmlContent / textContent / smsBody, none of which are columns of `campaigns` — so both the email and SMS send paths fell through to `campaign.name` and every recipient received the campaign's INTERNAL NAME instead of the body the customer composed in `campaigns.content`. The ninth was `(campaign as any).subject`, where `subject` IS a real column: a spurious cast, removed because an unnecessary `as any` is precisely how the eight beside it went unnoticed. Deletion-revealed by the ghost-field sweep (ledger 64), not a typing pass. Locked in per the strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 1347 -> 1335 on 2026-08-21: twelve casts went with the seller-motivation refusal in server/routes-epic-services.ts. Every one read a column that does not exist — assessedValue (on properties, and leads has no propertyId), ownerName, ownerState, ownershipYears, lastSalePrice, taxDelinquentYears, taxDelinquentAmount (the last six are on NO table) — each with a default that reads like a measurement, so the endpoint scored every lead in every org from the same invented vector and returned at most two distinct results. Deletion-revealed by the ghost-field sweep the auditOrgUsury fix prompted, not a typing pass. Locked in per the strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 1349 -> 1347 on 2026-08-21: both casts removed from auditOrgUsury in server/services/usury.ts, and neither was a typing nicety — they were the reason the defect compiled. `(note as any).propertyState` read a column that does not exist in shared/schema.ts, so it was `undefined` on every row and the `|| "TX"` fallback fired every time: every note in every organization was audited against Texas law and served as that org's compliance status by GET /api/compliance/usury-audit. `(note as any).borrowerName` was the same shape — `notes` carries `borrowerId` — so every row reported a null borrower. Replaced by a real org-scoped join to properties.state and leads. A cast on a field that does not exist reads as defensive and is the opposite; same pattern CLAUDE.md records from leads.organizationId. Locked in per the strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 1353 -> 1349 on 2026-08-21: deletion-revealed, not a typing improvement. Four casts went with the PropStream removal (deletion ledger, 2026-08-21) — the two `args as any` in the propstream_lookup / propstream_comps dispatch branches in server/ai/tools.ts, and two `(creds as any).mlsUrl` reads in services/connectors/executor.ts that the new `resoBaseUrl(creds)` helper replaced with a typed narrowing. The remaining connector dispatch branches keep their `args as any` and stay in this baseline; they are still reachable. Locked in per the strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 1354 -> 1353 on 2026-08-20: the dispatch branch for `batch_leads_skip_trace` in server/ai/tools.ts carried `args as any`, and the branch was deleted with the executor behind it (deletion ledger, 2026-08-20). Deletion-revealed, not a typing improvement: the FCRA gate added the day before returns before that switch, so the branch had been unreachable since it landed, and Pax was the executor's only caller. The four sibling connector branches keep their `args as any` and stay in this baseline — they are still reachable. Locked in per the strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 1355 -> 1354 on 2026-08-19: deletion-revealed, not a refactor. `atlasContextInjector.ts`, `communicationDeduplication.ts` and `userAiCostControls.ts` were deleted (deletion ledger 2026-08-19) after lint-reachability was taught to strip comments and showed all three were module orphans — each had been reading as imported because its own docblock opened with a usage example the scanner took for real code. Two of the three carried the same lazy-Redis shape (`let _redis: any`, `Promise<any | null>`, `const IORedis = (await import("ioredis")).default`), which is where these counts came from. Locked in per the strictly-down rule: the reduction belongs to the commit that earned it.  PRIOR NOTE — 1356 -> 1355 on 2026-08-19: routes-data-intelligence reads organizations.underwritingDefaults through its declared $type instead of casting to any, so a renamed section is a type error rather than a silent undefined. The landDeal section added in the same commit needed no cast for the same reason.
minimaNote: VACUITY FLOOR on the SCAN POPULATION, not a ratchet. baselineCount above counts BAD THINGS FOUND, so a scan that stops seeing files finds zero and reports it as progress: a zero baseline PASSes on an empty file set, and a nonzero one prints a stale-high "lock it in" for a number that was never true. MEASURED 2026-08-16: this config matched 1370 file(s) (server/**/*.ts minus tests). Floor set to 1100, comfortably below that, so a broken glob or walk trips it while ordinary deletion does not. Checked BEFORE the baseline comparison by scripts/ratchet.mjs; a MISSING floor fails as loudly as a breached one. If a real deletion wave shrinks this population, lower the floor in the same commit and name the wave here — never raise it to silence something, never delete the key. Re-measure with `node scripts/ratchet.mjs --measure`.
